chunks: From him, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the affluent man who acquires many clothes, new ones, the pallium (a type of cloak), and many shirts, preserving one set by another, beautifying himself with them. Would he be considered extravagant? He said: No, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Let him who has abundance spend out of his abundance.'

key_terms.الطَّيَالِسَةَ: A type of cloak or outer garment
key_terms.الْجِيَادَ: New clothes (specifically those not yet worn)
key_terms.يَصُونُ بَعْضُهَا بَعْضاً: Preserving one set by another (keeping them in good condition by rotation)

ai.seo_question: Is buying multiple sets of expensive clothes considered extravagance in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that accumulating multiple sets of fine garments for preservation and beautification does not constitute *israf* (wastefulness), provided it aligns with one's financial capacity. He supports this by citing Surah At-Talaq 65:7, interpreting the command for the wealthy to spend 'from their abundance' as a permission to enjoy and preserve quality goods rather than a mandate for austerity. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that luxury is permissible for the affluent as long as it does not lead to neglect of duties or excessive hoarding.
